summary: The RR scheduler with quantum=10 ran 5 processes with no preemptions, giving each process a fair share of CPU time. Process 4 ran immediately at time 0, while processes 5-8 arrived later and waited briefly before running.
main_reason: The quantum of 10 was large enough to complete each process's entire execution in a single time slice, eliminating preemptions and ensuring fair allocation.
evidence: RR algorithm with quantum=10 executed 5 processes
Process 4 arrived at 0 and exited at 4
Process 5 arrived at 2, first run at 4, exited at 5
Process 6 arrived at 5, first run at 5, exited at 7
Process 7 arrived at 10, first run at 10, exited at 14
Process 8 arrived at 15, first run at 15, exited at 16
suggestion: MLFQ with smaller quanta (2, 4, 8) would likely perform better by reducing avg_response_time to 0.0 and avg_waiting_time to 0.2, as it can prioritize shorter jobs and adapt to varying burst lengths.
